title: Handley Page Halifax LK930
memorial_details: Upright, rectangular, rough-hewn stone with brass plaque. Dedication is incised with white-painted, capital letters. Stone is surrounded by white kerbstones and granite chippings. Around 2020 a second plaque (possibly laminated plastic) mounted on a post was added, commemorating civilians involved in rescue attempts in the burning aircraft. The dedication is in black capital letters on a white background.
inscription: IN RECOGNITION OF/ THE 7 MAN CREW OF HALIFAX/ (LK930) NO 1664 HCU SQUADRON/ DISHFORTH/ WHICH CRASHED AT THIS POINT/ ON 22 MARCH 1944/ WITH THE LOSS OF 3 LIVES
community_connection: Civilians attempted rescue from the burning aircraft and are commemorated on a second plaque added to the memorial around 2020.

sources.title: Facebook post by Tony Hibberd (admin, RAF Bomber Command Memorials group), citing Chorley BCL Vol 8

narrative: On the night of 22 March 1944, Halifax LK930 of 1664 Heavy Conversion Unit, based at RAF Dishforth, crashed on the minor road between Palterton and Scarcliffe in Derbyshire while on a night cross-country navigation exercise. The aircraft went down for unknown reasons. Three of the seven crew were killed; four were injured. Civilians who attempted rescue from the burning wreck were later commemorated by a second plaque added to the memorial around 2020.
